text:
maya: Heads up — gitops sync failed for eu-west-1-gpu-cluster during the nodegroup rollout. Argo marked the app OutOfSync and failed with a pre-sync hook error, blocking the new nodegroup. @eng-oncall can you take a look? :grimacing:

sam: I pulled the argocd logs, looks like terraform wants to replace the launch template for the gpu nodegroup. Not sure what changed in repo, we didn't modify LT regionally.

leo: I saw an autoscaler event earlier this morning — spot pools were added and some nodes got tainted for GPU scheduling. Could be a lifecycle hook mismatch.

natalie: Pasted the relevant snippets below from our pipeline and Argo:
```
ArgoCD: rpc error: code = Aborted desc = pre-sync hook failed: job "nodegroup-preflight" failed with exit code 1
Terraform plan: ~ module.gpu_node_group.aws_launch_template.this (forces replacement)
  - user_data: (sensitive) => (known after apply)
  - iam_instance_profile: "gw-gpu-profile-v3" => "gw-gpu-profile-v4"
```

sam: Hmm, IAM profile version bump would trigger replacement. Who updated the module inputs? Could be a merge from the infra-bump branch.

maya: The immediate problem is Argo holding the sync because the pre-sync job expects nodes with taint gpu=true:NoSchedule to be present. New nodegroup replacement removes taint init script until after join, so the job times out. That blocks the Helm/cni upgrade we also queued.

leo: Quick mitigation: we can manually mark the argocd app as synced and proceed with the rollout, but that risks partial state if TF replaces nodes mid-traffic. Alternative is to rollback the commit that bumped the iam profile and rerun.

natalie: Cost note — if TF replaces the whole nodegroup we'll spin up new GPU instances (p4/ga100) then drain+terminate old ones: huge cost spike for the hour. We should avoid full replacement in peak business hours.

eng-oncall: I'm on it. Steps I'll try: 1) Pause Argo sync for the app, 2) run `kubectl cordon` on the drained nodes we control, 3) apply a tiny patch to the pre-sync job to increase timeout and accept missing taints, 4) open a rollback PR for the LT change.

maya: Please also check GitOps pipeline so we don't re-trigger terraform apply from CI while manual fixes are in progress. Add a hold on the pipeline run.

sam: For longer term: we should make the pre-sync job resilient to node replacement by using label-based detection instead of immediate taint checks. Also add a plan-only gate in Argo that surfaces TF replace operations (like launch_template replacements) and requires manual approval for destructive changes.

leo: Agree. Plus add a quick sanity check in our GitHub Actions that compares old/new iam_instance_profile and warns if replace will happen. Could be an automated PR comment.

natalie: Patch I just pushed to the infra branch increases the pre-sync timeout and falls back to a soft warning instead of hard fail. Pushed to staging. Please hold on terraform applies until we confirm Argo behaves.

argocd-bot: Application "eu-west-1/gpu-cluster" sync paused by natalie at 1762001301.

maya: TL;DR action items: @eng-oncall manual pause + cordon, natalie landed a soft-fail patch, sam to add manual-approval gate for destructive TF plans, leo to add CI diff check, and we avoid terraform apply during the window.

sam: I'll create the approval gate RFC and a small GH Actions check today.

leo: I'll prototype the diff check and a terraform plan parser that flags `forces replacement` for aws_launch_template and nodegroup resources.

eng-oncall: Done pausing Argo and cordoning two nodes. Watching the pre-sync job now — it retried and passed once the timeout was bumped. Rolling the rest carefully.

maya: Great work team. After rollout let's run a quick cost audit for the hour and add notes to the runbook about LT/iam profile bumps and pre-sync behavior. :thumbsup:
